title: Dashboard Boarding Pass — lightweight onboarding notes for inference dashboards
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, actionable onboarding crib sheet for engineers who need to stand up or modify inference dashboards quickly. Not a replacement for the full playbooks — but something you can bookmark and copy-paste from when you only have 30–90 minutes to ship a useful dashboard.

Audience:
- PMs and engineers owning a model route or feature
- SREs who need an ops-facing view with alert anchors
- Solutions/SEs who want a customer-facing SLA view (smaller, curated subset)

Principles (keep dashboards small and useful):
- Start with the golden 5: request rate, p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost per request, successful inference count.
- Three lanes: user-impact (top), infra/serving (middle), economics (bottom).
- Query cost limit: every widget should be sub-second in dev dashboards; use pre-aggregated metrics in prod.
- Use tenant or route-level filters at the top of the dashboard.
- If a metric can be misunderstood, add a one-line description in the widget hover text.

Metric definitions (copy-ready lines):
- requests_per_minute: count(requests) by 1m where route = <ROUTE_NAME> and status != 429; unit: req/min.
- p95_inference_latency_ms: 95th_percentile(latency_ms) computed on server-side span end - span start; exclude warmup/batch-hold durations; window: 5m.
- p50_inference_latency_ms: median(latency_ms) same as above; window: 5m.
- error_rate_percent: 100 * count(status >= 500) / count(status >= 200) over 5m; alert when > 2% sustained 5m.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: 100 * sum(kv_cache_hits) / (sum(kv_cache_hits) + sum(kv_cache_misses)); note: only accurate if instrumented per-model cache key.
- tokens_per_request: sum(output_tokens + input_tokens) / count(requests) for route; use rolling 1h to smooth.
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: derived from billing price table; surface as annotation not raw telemetry.
- concurrent_inflight_requests: gauge of inflight requests per host; useful for autoscaler tuning.

Span & tracing guidelines (pragmatic):
- Naming convention: inference.request (root), model.compile (optional), runtime.kvcache.lookup, runtime.kernel.exec, runtime.response.serialize. Keep prefix 'runtime.' for low-level spans.
- Add these tags/attributes on root span: route, model_name, model_version, tenant_id (if multi-tenant), request_id, batch_size, sequence_length_hint.
- Sampling: default adaptive sampling at 0.5% of requests + 100% of requests with status >= 500 or latency > p95*1.5.
- Breadcrumbs: emit a short compact timeline of span names as a single attribute on root span to help fast triage in UIs that don't show full trees. Format: "r:runtime.kvcache.lookup,k:runtime.kernel.exec,s:runtime.response.serialize".
- Span duration attribution: prefer recorded durations at span end; if batch batching hides per-request timings, compute a per-request estimate in logs and tag it.

Dashboard layout template (column order):
1) Top ribbon: route selector, environment, start/end, tenant selector.
2) Row 1 (user impact): requests_per_minute, success_rate (1-error_rate), p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, small sparklines of last 1h.
3) Row 2 (errors & traces): error_rate_percent, dominant_error_codes (top N), quick-trace link widget that opens traced request sample; a list of recent annotated spans for failures.
4) Row 3 (serving infra): concurrent_inflight_requests, avg_batch_size, queue_time_ms, model_cpu_util_pct, model_gpu_util_pct.
5) Row 4 (caching & batching): kv_cache_hit_ratio, cache_evictions_per_min, effective_batching_ratio (requests combined / requests_received).
6) Row 5 (cost & capacity): tokens_per_request, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd (annotated), estimated_usd_per_hour_rl (computed from throughput * cost).
7) Bottom: runbook links, ownership, last deploy tag, linked PR/commit.

Widget tips and query patterns:
- Use pre-aggregated counters for high-cardinality routes; fall back to sampled histograms for latency.
- For p95 compute: use histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(latency_bucket[5m])) — ensure buckets align across services.
- To avoid query explosion: always inject route=~"(routeA|routeB|routeC)" when building operator dashboards.
- Sparklines: compute against shorter window (1h) and show delta.

Alerting anchors (example SLO mapping):
- SLO: 99.5% of requests under 500ms p95 over 30d. Alert: burn rate > 6x for 1h or sustained error_rate_percent > 1% for 15m.
- Immediate pager: error_rate_percent > 5% for 5m OR p95_inference_latency_ms > 1.5s for 5m.
- Ops page: kv_cache_hit_ratio drops > 20 percentage points relative to baseline for 10m.

Sampling & cost control suggestions:
- Export full traces only for sampled requests; always emit compact root span attributes so trace-less requests still surface key data in logs/metrics.
- Use a trace-to-metric bridge: for sampled traces, increment counters for new error types to catch unknown failure modes.
- If widget queries are expensive, create precomputed rollup jobs (1m/5m) with labels adjusted (no tenant-level fine-grained tag unless necessary).

Quick experiments to run after dashboard is live (10–30 min each):
- Flip adaptive sampling to 1% for 30m and see if we capture different failure modes.
- Temporarily increase kv cache instrumentation to emit debug counters for a small tenant and observe hit ratio changes.
- Add a synthetic traffic canary (slow path and fast path) and create synthetic traces to map latency tail causes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want tenant-aware cost POC in dashboard or keep cost in Console only? (ask product)
- How to represent batched-request attribution cleanly in traces without exploding span cardinality? Proposal: per-batch root span with per-request minimal attributes and a light per-request log message.
- Standardize histogram bucket edges for latency across runtime components (SLO depends on this).

Runbook snippets (copy/paste):
- If p95 spikes: check successful_request_count vs total, open quick-trace for p95 examples, check model eviction logs and kernel failures in the last 10m.
- If error_rate rises: filter by error code; if 5xx across hosts, suspect model or runtime; check model-serving logs and GPU OOMs; if 429, investigate rate-limiter or autoscaler thresholds.

Notes to self (small reminders):
- For customer-facing dashboards, collapse infra rows and expose only user-impact + cost summary + runbook link.
- Keep widget naming consistent: prefix metric with short area name (e.g., "lat[p95] / route=..." or "cost[1k] / route").

References and quick links:
- Confluence quickstart: OBS-quickstart-2025 (linked above)
- Example dashboard template repo: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/widget-templates

Last updated: 2026-03-01 by Aisha.
Notes: treat this as a lightweight companion to the full Observability Playbook; will iterate into a template JSON for the dashboard repo when we validate fields with Platform telemetry.
